title: Acquisition
description: Choose, document and verify proportionate digital evidence acquisitions. Compare the source interface, addressable extent and stored result using the C09 file-based fixtures.

lessons.title: Imaging concepts
lessons.summary: Choose an acquisition boundary and interpret a verification receipt for a synthetic source, master and review copy.
objectives: Distinguish device, volume and file-level acquisition boundaries.
Interpret the supplied C09 acquisition transcript and explain the limits of matching hashes.
Write an acquisition receipt that identifies scope, errors, excluded evidence and the verification method.

lessons.title: Write blockers
lessons.summary: How hardware and software write blockers protect a source device during acquisition, what they cannot protect, and how a laboratory tests and records a specific unit before relying on it.
objectives: Explain how a write blocker forwards, stops and relays commands at the storage interface
Distinguish hardware and software write blockers from read-only mounting and media lock switches
Identify acquisition risks that lie outside a write blocker's control
Plan and record a pre-use check of a specific blocker unit and firmware
Review a fictional acquisition receipt against the original kit transcript and report discrepancies

lessons.title: Hashing
lessons.summary: How cryptographic hashes verify forensic images and copies, what a matching digest does and does not establish, and how to record values and handle mismatches without altering the record.
objectives: Explain preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance and why they rule out MD5 and SHA-1 as primary values
Interpret the hash checkpoints in the C09 acquisition transcript, including the one-byte mismatch
Distinguish what a matching digest establishes from what needs separate records
Apply a fixed mismatch procedure that preserves the original record
Perform and document offline file-based verification of an image or copy

lessons.title: E01 and raw formats
lessons.summary: How raw (dd) and Expert Witness (E01) images store the same media stream differently, and why only a media hash, never a container hash, can be compared with the acquisition record.
objectives: Distinguish the media stream from the container for raw, split raw and E01 images
Explain the main E01 sections, chunking, compression and checksums, and what each can and cannot prove
Select the correct verification method for a given format and recognise a container-versus-media hash false alarm
Interpret the kit's raw acquisition transcript and reason about an E01 of the same stream without inventing output
Justify a format choice and document conversions as new, separately verified copies

lessons.title: Live vs dead acquisition
lessons.summary: How to choose between acquiring a system while running or powered off, what each mode preserves and destroys, why a hash proves different things in each, and how to review the acquisition record that justifies the choice.
objectives: Compare dead and live acquisition by repeatability, coverage, examiner footprint and dependence on the suspect operating system
Explain why a live capture's digest protects only the output file while a static image's digest can be compared with the source
Apply a documented decision path covering power state, volatile data in scope, shutdown method and systems that cannot go offline
Interpret the original static-acquisition transcript and identify what it can and cannot show
Review fictional acquisition records for overstated integrity claims, missing limitations and missing clock references
